description: GHEDesigner designs ground heat exchangers for ground-source heat-pump systems. Oklahoma State University and U.S. national-laboratory contributors publish Python source, documentation and design examples. A user supplies property boundaries, no-drill areas, heating and cooling loads, ground properties, borehole geometry and system settings. The program places and sizes boreholes and can simulate district-scale loops, buildings, heat pumps and horizontal distribution piping. Outputs include a proposed borehole field and thermal design results for the selected site and load period. Geographic coverage is site-specific; the time horizon follows the hourly load profile and design settings. The source is free under a BSD-style three-clause licence with a U.S. Department of Energy rights notice. A limitation is that borehole sizing depends on local ground properties and load estimates; the tool does not supply those measurements. It supports district heating and building-energy capacity studies. The catalogue's model-energyplus can supply building-load context, but no data exchange was tested. No example or ground dataset was downloaded.
